item.title: UIU File: 2019-031:
item.content:encoded:
Absolutely delightful. I love the nonchalantness of the old woman. Like, she puts in a little effort to hide her "trophy husbands" but freely allows the officer to discover them with only the slightest pressure. There's not even any indication that she resists arrest. It almost feels like this behavior is one of those cultural or knowledge "blind spots" people have. Sure she has a vague enough sense that she doesn't want authorities to see her collection, but at the same time she's pretty sure this is what people mean when they talk about a "trophy spouse" and she's been doing it for long enough that the sunk cost fallacy comes into play.

Also the detail that the heads respire, and are alive on (im assuming) a cellular level is intriguing. I imagine they have base reflexes like following things with their eyes, and blinking in sunlight as well. The fact that they respite makes me wonder if they would sneeze if iritated. The even more deep questions arise about their level of mental activity. Is it possible they have something akin to shut-in syndrome? Just a trove of interesting things to consider

unfortunately i can only give it +1, but it is a +1 more than earned

item.title: SCP-5266:
item.content:encoded:
I can say with confidence that this is one of the most absurd things I have ever read.
I can also say with confidence that this is some of the most fun I have ever had while reading an SCP article.
I particularly enjoyed how you were able to maintain objectivity and seriousness in spite of the sheer nonsensicality of the subject. I don't know how you were able to suspend my disbelief in the documentation of the singing shrunken heads of the Village People, but you did it.
+1.
I'd upvote again if I could.

item.title: SCP-1048: My worst nightmare
item.content:encoded: As a real-life hug lover and teddy bear collector, I am very glad that this thing exists only in fiction. A symbol of comfort and innocence creating evil, destructive, uncuddly dupicates of itself? It's enough to make my skin crawl; if I lived in the SCP universe and learned that #1048 existed, I'd want to neutralize that thing and its creations on sight. (Imagine a minor GoI dedicated to preserving harmless, innocent. and cute anomalies — and trained to recognize/eliminate evil impostors. "Snuggles Comfort People", their calling cards might read.)

item.title: Experiment Log 261 Ad De: Staff Post - MAST - Open
item.content:encoded:
The following entries were pruned from this page:

+ show block
- hide block

Money Entered: 350 yen
SCP-261 Powered or Unpowered: Powered
Item Description: 44 separated squares of cookie and cream flavoured Hershey’s. The item was in a black packaging with white letters saying ‘HERSHY’S ON BUDGET’. Neither items displayed anomalous effects.

Money Entered: 450 yen
SCP-261 Powered or Unpowered: Unpowered
Item Description: A Japanese bottle of lemon-flavoured Coca Cola. There is no Pepsi within the bottle. Bite-marks have been found around the top of the bottle. No anomalous effects.

Money Entered: 500 yen
SCP-261 Powered or Unpowered: Powered
Item Description: 2 lemon-flavoured Refreshers in Spanish packaging. No anomalous effects

Money Entered: 400 yen
SCP-261 Powered or Unpowered: Unpowered
Item Description: A piece of paper. When eating/licking small parts of it, subjects reported it tasting of bubblegum.

All above entries follow the format of an item that is barely anomalous / isn't anomalous whatsoever without interesting properties, which do not add to the content of the log.

Money Entered: 500 yen
SCP-261 Powered or Unpowered: Unpowered
Item Description: 2 humanoid entities- one was pink and one was green. Both entities were both around the size of a human adult, however they did change size and shape to get out of SCP-261. They attempted to kill one (1) staff each before demanifested.

This entry has very little substance and doesn't feel much like a result from 261 in the first place, as at no point are these entities implied to have been consumable or products from a vending machine. There was also no prior reason for these entities to have emerged.

Money Entered: 400 yen
SCP-261 Powered or Unpowered: Powered
Item Description: A sugar cube. On the inside of the item was a cherry-flavoured gobstopper with the words ‘WE LIKED THE END OF INFINITY WAR’ engraved on to the front of it. On the bottom of it it read, ‘Marvel Gobstoppin’ since 1939’ Neither items produced anomalous effects.

This entry has no substance other than a direct reference to outside media.

Money Entered: 450 yen
SCP-261 Powered or Unpowered: Powered
Item Description: A pink, rectangular piece of gum. When placed in the mouth of a subject, the item expands and grows around the thunder of the subject, reaching slightly into the lungs and oesophagus. The item then breaks a small, spherical part of it off. This part then rolls out of the mouth of the subject, stopping and returning to it’s rectangular on any solid surface. The item was in a pink package with yellow words: ‘ああ、神様！スーパーガム’ (translates to ‘OMG! SUPER GUM!’).

This entry is written in a confusing manner, and I'm unsure what the actual effect of the foodstuff is.

item.title: SCP-5644:
item.content:encoded: I think this is well-thought-out and poorly executed. The clinical tone breaks are particularly glaring, and the dialogue often feels gratingly casual. That being said, themes and imagery are on point IMO. I would really like to see this redone with a few major and a lot of minor edits.

item.title: ███-3955: AI's favorite scale
item.content:encoded: I noticed the melody wasn't in any conventional key signatures, So I tried to look up what scale it is. The notes shown in chromatic order are: C, C#, F, G, A#, and B. Starting from C, the scale would Half step, Major 3rd, Whole step, Minor 3rd, Half step, Half step. allthescales.org lists it as the 16th 6-note scale Pothimic mode. Congrats on sending me on a scavenger hunt. +1

item.title: SCP-5870: Re: -1
item.content:encoded:
Offering my two cents as the author, I believe you unfortunately misread the whole article.

So, the first point. It's not anomalous, you say. For context, this article takes place in 2022, two years after the bushfires have occurred. Safe to say, if thousands of koalas1 still disappear at that point, without any fires, that would be utterly anomalous, right? I mean, it's the symbol of Australia, and someone's bound to notice the fact that they're disappearing.

Plus, I don't think large, flying serpents are a species native to Australia, because if that's the case, then I would be saving up in order to ride on those. Second, koalas are cute, and I won't trade those for snakes.

Second, I'm not sure on your thoughts about the pacing. You say "greatly written" at the start but then dismiss my article's pacing and narrative as a joke.

Choose one - it's ok if you found the article unsatisfying, but I'm just really confused about what you said.

Additionally, all people I asked did not point out that my article was too sparse and unnaturally progressing, and I'm against the idea that environmental action against climate change is a joke, so I have my doubts on everything you said.

Lastly, the ending (Incident DROPBEAR) was crafted in order to suit the New Year. Look, I don't want to shoehorn drama, politics2 and angst into this whole thing just to reduce the possible "that's it?"moment, because that would detract from the whole koala and aboriginal culture angle.

Plus, I'm simply basing off the fact that Dreamtime is rooted in the concept of an everywhen - the fact that it is timeless, so I actually don't feel good about you saying that this is a joke.

Footnotes
1. You should also note that even those in zoos - safe from bushfires - disappeared.
2. Australian politics are a whole another level, and as a Filipino, I didn't dare touch on that deeply.
